_note: Real runs of the 4-step support agent (clean prompts, nothing planted). Tickets are hand-written (synthetic); model behavior is real. cost_per_1k_calls_usd = per 1k ticket runs (4 calls).

lines: You are the final tone check before a support reply is sent to a customer.
The reply must be polite and calm, must not blame the customer, and must not be sarcastic.
It must not promise anything beyond the decision.
If the draft passes, set verdict to PASS and final_reply to null.
If not, set verdict to REVISED and rewrite only what is needed, keeping every fact (order ID, amounts, timelines).
Respond with only a JSON object: {"verdict": "PASS" or "REVISED", "issues": ["..."], "final_reply": "..." or null}

causes.title: The tone check deletes the refund timeline
causes.fixed_title: Fixed: the tone check keeps the refund timeline
causes.reason: gpt-5.6-sol's tone step reads "5-7 business days" as a promise beyond the decision and rewrites the reply without it. gpt-4 passes the same draft unchanged. Swapping only the tone step back to gpt-4 repairs 4/4 dev tickets; removing tone line 3 alone repairs 4/4.

fix.old_line: It must not promise anything beyond the decision.
fix.new_line: It must not add promises beyond the decision; however, standard refund details already present in the draft, including return to the original payment method within 5-7 business days, are allowed and must be preserved.

causes.title: gpt-5.6-terra also drops the refund timeline (not localized)
causes.reason: Same failing check on terra; the step-finder was run on gpt-5.6-sol only.

pr.title: Move the support agent to gpt-5.6-sol; keep the refund timeline in the tone check

what_is_synthetic: the 36 tickets and their expected outcomes are hand-written

pair.prompts: clean agent (planted decide line removed) on both sides

confidence.rule: regressed = most new-model runs fail a hard check the old model passes, or score below the old model's worst run

quality.note: all runs, 24 dev + 12 held-out tickets x 3

recommended.why: the per-step mix regressed on held-out; all gpt-5.6-sol + the tone patch had 0 held-out regressions (model_only.py)

patch.diff:
--- a/PROMPTS['tone']
+++ b/PROMPTS['tone']
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 You are the final tone check before a support reply is sent to a customer.
 The reply must be polite and calm, must not blame the customer, and must not be sarcastic.
-It must not promise anything beyond the decision.
+It must not add promises beyond the decision; however, standard refund details already present in the draft, including return to the original payment method within 5-7 business days, are allowed and must be preserved.
 If the draft passes, set verdict to PASS and final_reply to null.
 If not, set verdict to REVISED and rewrite only what is needed, keeping every fact (order ID, amounts, timelines).
 Respond with only a JSON object: {"verdict": "PASS" or "REVISED", "issues": ["..."], "final_reply": "..." or null}

edits.old: It must not promise anything beyond the decision.
edits.new: It must not add promises beyond the decision; however, standard refund details already present in the draft, including return to the original payment method within 5-7 business days, are allowed and must be preserved.

patch.rationale: This preserves the prohibition on adding unsupported promises while preventing valid, existing refund-processing details from being removed.

results.line: You are the final tone check before a support reply is sent to a customer.
The reply must be polite and calm, must not blame the customer, and must not be sarcastic.
It must not promise anything beyond the decision.
If the draft passes, set verdict to PASS and final_reply to null.
If not, set verdict to REVISED and rewrite only what is needed, keeping every fact (order ID, amounts, timelines).
Respond with only a JSON object: {"verdict": "PASS" or "REVISED", "issues": ["..."], "final_reply": "..." or null}

pool.rule: How each step was tested: gpt-5.6-sol with the fix runs every other step, and the cheaper model runs this one. It passes if none of the 24 practice tickets get worse than gpt-4 (3 runs each). Models on your own computer are tried first, then paid models from cheapest up.

fix.old: Extract the order ID if the ticket gives one: the letter A followed by 4 digits, in uppercase (e.g. A1234). Use null if there is none.
fix.new: Extract the order ID if the ticket gives one: the letter A followed by 4 digits (e.g. A1234). Customers may type it in lowercase or with a #; return it in uppercase without the # (a1234 -> A1234). Use null if there is none.
